paper.title: Fast Rates for Bandit Optimization with Upper-Confidence Frank-Wolfe

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit optimization over the simplex, C-smooth convex loss
unmapped: Learner picks one of K actions each round; the decision variable is the vector of empirical action proportions p_T in the simplex, objective is the global loss L(p_T) - min L (not a cumulative loss)
Feedback: after choosing action i, a noisy estimate of the gradient of L at p_t whose i-th coordinate has deviation alpha_{t,i}(T_i, delta) = 2 sqrt(log(t/delta)/T_i)
settings.definition_quote: A each time step $t \ge 1$, a decision maker chooses an action $\pi_t \in [K]$ from $K$ different actions with the objective of minimizing an unknown convex loss function $L: \Delta_K \to \R$. ... rather to minimize the global loss $L(p_T)$ ... $r(T):= \E[L(p_T)] - \min_{p \in \Delta_K} L(p)$. The information available to the policy is a feedback of bandit type: given the choice $\pi_t = i$, it is an estimate $\hat g_{t}$ of $\nabla L(p_t)$.

Denoting by $\mu_i$ the expected loss of arm $i \in [K]$, the average pseudo-regret $\bar R$ can be expressed as $\bar R(t) = \frac{1}{t} \sum_{s=1}^t \mu_{\pi_s} - \mu^*$ ... Hence the choice of $L(\mu,p) = \mu^\top p$ corresponds the problem of multi-armed bandits.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit optimization, C-smooth mu-strongly convex loss with interior minimum
unmapped: Objective is global loss of empirical action proportions L(p_T) - min L
Feedback: noisy gradient estimate with coordinate-wise deviation 2 sqrt(log(t/delta)/T_i)
settings.definition_quote: Let $L:\Delta_K \rightarrow \R$ be a $C$-smooth, $\mu$-strongly convex function such that its minimum $p_\star$ satisfies $\dist(p_\star,\partial \Delta_K) \ge \eta$

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit optimization over linear forms (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is global loss of the output/proportion vector p_T
Feedback: draw from a distribution with mean mu_i when action i is chosen (gradient coordinate feedback)
settings.definition_quote: This result is established over the class of linear functions over the simplex (for which $C=0$), when the feedback consists of a draw from a distribution with mean $\mu_i$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit optimization over 1-strongly convex functions (lower bound)
unmapped: Objective is global loss of output p_T; feedback for action i is a N(theta_i,1) draw giving the i-th gradient coordinate
settings.definition_quote: we have over the class $\cS_{1,K}$ of $1$-strongly convex functions ... The proof relies on the complexity of minimizing quadratic functions $\frac{1}{2}\|p-\theta\|_2^2$ when observing a draw from distribution with mean $\theta_i$.

source.label: THM:slow
source.quote: Let $L$ be a $C$-smooth convex function over the unit simplex $\Delta_K$. For any $T \ge 1$, after $T$ steps of the UCB Frank-Wolfe algorithm with a bandit feedback such that $\alpha_{t,i}(T_i,\delta)=2\sqrt{\log(t/\delta)/T_i}$ and the choice $\delta_t=1/t^2$, it holds that \E[L(p_T)] - L(p_\star) \le 4 \sqrt{\frac{3K \log(T)}{T}} +\frac{C\log(eT)}{T}+(\frac{\pi^2}{6}+K)\frac{2\|\nabla L\|_\infty+\|L\|_\infty}{T}.

results.notes: Quantity is the optimization error E[L(p_T)] - min L of the empirical proportions (not cumulative regret), hence 'other'. Algorithm does not use T, so anytime.

symbols.mu_inf: sup norm of the mean loss vector mu

conditions: feedback deviation alpha_{t,i}(T_i,delta)=2 sqrt(log(t/delta)/T_i)
losses (minimisation): Delta_i = mu_i - mu_star

source.label: PRO:fastbandit
source.quote: Let $L$ be the linear function $p\mapsto p^\top\mu $. After $T$ steps of the UCB Frank-Wolfe algorithm with a bandit feedback such that $\alpha_{t,i}(T_i,\delta)=2\sqrt{\log(t/\delta)/T_i}$, the choices of $\delta_t=1/t^2$ hold the following \E[L(p_T)] - L(p_\star) \le \frac{48 \log(T)}{T} \sum_{i \neq \star} \frac{1}{\Delta^{(i)}} +3\Big(\frac{\pi^2}{3}+K\Big)\frac{\sqrt{K}\|\mu\|_\infty}{T}

results.notes: Paper bounds the average pseudo-regret; multiplied by T to give the total pseudo-regret.

source.label: THM:faststrong
source.quote: Let $L:\Delta_K \rightarrow \R$ be a $C$-smooth, $\mu$-strongly convex function such that its minimum $p_\star$ satisfies $\dist(p_\star,\partial \Delta_K) \ge \eta$, for some $\eta \in (0,1/K]$. After $T$ steps of the UCB Frank-Wolfe algorithm ... with the choice of $\delta_t =1/t^2$, \E[L(p_T)] - L(p_\star) \le c_1 \frac{\log^2(T)}{T} + c_2\frac{\log(T)}{T} + c_3 \frac{1}{T}, for constants $c_1=\frac{96K}{\mu\eta^2}$, $c_2=\frac{24}{\mu\eta^3}+C$ and $c_3=24(\frac{20}{\mu\eta^2})^2K+\frac{\mu\eta^2}{2}+C$.

results.notes: Proof first assumes known horizon then gives an anytime variant via a doubling-trick-in-the-analysis argument; constants in the appendix differ from the theorem statement. Recorded as stated.

source.label: THM:lowslow
source.quote: For any algorithm based on a bandit feedback such that $\alpha_{t,i}(T_i,\delta)=\sqrt{2\log(t/\delta)/T_i}$ and that outputs $\hat p_T$, we have over the class of linear forms $\mathcal{L}_K$ that for some constant $c>0$ \inf_{\hat p_T} \sup_{L \in \mathcal{L}_{K}} \{\E[L(\hat p_T)] - L(p_\star) \} \ge c \sqrt{K/T}.

results.notes: Described as a direct corollary of the minimax lower bound of Auer et al. (ACFS03) for multi-armed bandits (average regret).

bound.expression_latex: \inf_{\hat p} \sup_{L \in \cS_{1,K}}\Big\{ \E[L(\hat p_T)] - L(p^\star) \Big\} \ge c \, K^2/ T

conditions: L ranges over 1-strongly convex functions on the simplex (hard instances: quadratics (1/2)||p-theta||^2)
feedback with deviation alpha_{t,i}(T_i,delta)=sqrt(2 log(t/delta)/T_i) (Gaussian N(theta_i,1) observations in proof)
proof requires K > 64 log(2)/nu, T > 4 nu^2 K^4 for some nu in (0,1/29), K even

source.label: THM:lowfast
source.quote: For any algorithm with a bandit feedback such that $\alpha_{t,i}(T_i,\delta)=\sqrt{2\log(t/\delta)/T_i}$ and output $\hat p_T$, we have over the class $\cS_{1,K}$ of $1$-strongly convex functions that for some constant $c>0$ \inf_{\hat p} \sup_{L \in \cS_{1,K}}\Big\{ \E[L(\hat p_T)] - L(p^\star) \Big\} \ge c \, K^2/ T.

results.notes: Conditions on K and T come from the proof, not the statement.

source.label: PRO:lowfastfeed
source.quote: For $L$ in the class of linear forms $\cF_3$ on $\Delta_3$, with a mixed bandit feedback we have \inf_{\hat p} \sup_{L \in \cF_{3}}\Big\{ \E[L(\hat p_T)] - L\theta(p^\star) \Big\} \ge c/T^{1/3}.

results.notes: No proof given; text says this follows from partial monitoring lower bounds (Cesa-Bianchi, Lugosi, Stoltz 2006). Label duplicated in source with Proposition 10.
